chunks: A group informed me, from Hārūn ibn Mūsā, from Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

My father ordered me to make the height of his grave four spread fingers, and he mentioned that sprinkling with water is good, and he said: Perform wudu (ablution) when you place the deceased into the grave.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: When the people depart from him, some of his brethren should remain behind at the grave and call out in the loudest voice: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, to the end of the talqin.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ أَصَابِعَ مُفَرَّجَاتٍ: a measurement of four spread fingers for the grave's height
key_terms.التَّلْقِينِ: prompting or instructing the deceased after burial
key_terms.اِرْتِفَاعَ قَبْرِهِ: the elevation or height of the grave

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the proper burial practices and talqin after burial in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This report discusses recommended practices related to burial: raising the grave to a measured height, sprinkling water upon it, and performing wudu (ablution) when placing the deceased in the grave. It also mentions the practice of talqin after burial, in which the deceased is addressed at the grave.
